chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not be deceived by the one who is skilled with the two forearms in bloodshed, for indeed he has with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a killer that does not die.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and what is a killer that does not die?' So he said: 'The Fire.'

key_terms.النَّارُ: The Fire — Hellfire, the ultimate and undying punishment prepared by Allah for the unjust
key_terms.رَحْبُ الذِّرَاعَيْنِ: Literally 'wide/broad of forearms', idiom for one skilled and strong in fighting or killing; a formidable warrior
key_terms.قَاتِلٌ لَا يَمُوتُ: A killer that does not die — metaphor for the eternal fire of Hell as the divine retribution awaiting murderers

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about those who are skilled at killing and their punishment in the afterlife?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the fourth Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS), records the Prophet's warning against being impressed or deceived by someone who is skilled at killing. The Prophet warns that such a killer will face a retribution that never ends — the eternal punishment of Hellfire. The phrase 'a killer that does not die' is a vivid metaphor for the everlasting nature of divine punishment, emphasizing that earthly power over life and death pales before the ultimate judgment of God.
